title: Returning to running postnatal – guidelines for medical, health and fitness professionals managing this population
publisher: Goom T, Donnelly G, Brockwell E (professional consensus guideline)
claims: Return to running is not advisable prior to 3 months postnatal, or beyond that time if any symptoms of pelvic floor dysfunction are identified before or after attempting a return to running.
Every postpartum mother, regardless of delivery mode, should be offered the opportunity to receive a pelvic health assessment with a specialist physiotherapist from 6 weeks postnatal.

Key signs or symptoms of pelvic floor or abdominal wall dysfunction include urinary or faecal incontinence, urgency difficult to defer, pelvic heaviness, pressure, bulge or dragging, pelvic or lumbopelvic pain, and a pendular abdomen or separated abdominal muscles.

If the readiness criteria are met after 3 months, a graded return can start small, around 1 to 2 minutes of easy running; build running volume before intensity, with weekly running distance or time increased by no more than around 10%.

The guideline is based on the best available evidence alongside experienced clinical opinion; it is designed to assist clinical reasoning rather than replace it, and it does not provide a prescriptive approach.
license: Professional guideline; citation and summary only
